nodes.name: journeys execute HTTP steps and stamp verdicts at the failing boundary

nodes.name: the next router serves the highest-priority asserted residue with a prompt contract

nodes.name: work packets are self-contained for a weak worker
nodes.description: a served item carries its read set with inline descriptions, stale causes, the truth gap, and a prompt contract with a prefilled write-back

nodes.name: the store is the single SQL write boundary
nodes.description: all SQL lives in the store; init/lock/migration, node CRUD and resolution, and derived-plane primitives enforce the truth-class and evidence gates at write time

nodes.name: quality packets pre-screen rule patterns into confirmable hits
nodes.description: rule regex patterns run over grounded files at packet-build time so the quality worker confirms or refutes concrete hits instead of searching

nodes.name: sync orchestrates seeded derivers behind a domain-blind seam
nodes.description: the engine iterates Deriver implementations over changed artifacts; code specifics live in the derivers and the ArtifactClass contract, never in sync

nodes.name: quality packs seed reusable norms with worked examples
nodes.description: shipped packs define QualityRule bodies with detection guidance and few-shot examples; seeding is idempotent and drift from the pack is detectable

nodes.name: commands are parsed once and dispatched to exactly one handler
nodes.description: clap parses the full surface into typed Command values; commands::run maps each variant to one handler; no handler parses arguments

nodes.name: finding gates are portable config calibrated from the repo
nodes.description: structural finding thresholds load from config with shipped defaults, travel in the export, and calibrate proposes worst-tail gates from the repo's own metric distribution

nodes.name: proposals decompose into numbered adoptable items
nodes.description: a captured proposal holds numbered items inside its body; adoption marks an item and can spawn a planned intent or task with the source recorded

nodes.name: the evidence policy travels as portable config
nodes.description: the review-confidence floor and human-gated lanes load from config.evidence_policy with shipped defaults and survive export/import

nodes.name: completeness scores a feature's surroundings across six axes
nodes.description: scenarios, prerequisites, boundary, proof, journey and questions compute per-intent from graph shape on read; waivers are explicit and reopen on redefinition

nodes.name: external diagnostics converge into derived findings
nodes.description: registered adapter commands run any language's linter; parsed diagnostics become derived Finding nodes; re-running resolves findings whose diagnostics disappeared

nodes.name: wiki pages stay fresh exactly while their documented scope holds
nodes.description: wiki plan grounds a page in intents, record stamps the documented scope fingerprint, and sync stales the page when a documented intent, its code or its proof drifts

nodes.name: every node and edge is typed by the model and edge-kind registry
nodes.description: NodeType/EdgeKind/TruthClass/InspectionStatus enums plus the per-kind endpoint registry make a mistyped edge unrepresentable at the boundary

nodes.name: signal-plane reads and finding adjudication share one command surface
nodes.description: smells, debt, findings, coverage, calibrate and threshold commands read computed signals; the only writes are durable finding adjudications and threshold config

nodes.name: import loads every node before any edge
nodes.description: two-phase restore: parse-and-validate the whole export, then in one transaction insert all nodes before any edge, so an edge endpoint always resolves

nodes.name: grounding and relationship edges are managed through typed commands
nodes.description: edge implement/relate/verdict/set-role/rehome/remove operate on registry-validated kinds with locators, roles and evidence-gated verdicts

nodes.name: validation lifecycle flows through evidence-gated proof commands
nodes.description: validation add/update/verdict/run and run --all mutate proofs only through the store's evidence gates; blocked requires a reason

nodes.name: hypotheses surfaces and vocabulary are captured as asserted domain knowledge
nodes.description: hypothesis add/prove/adopt/reject, interface surfaces, vocab and layer order record judgment-plane declarations that arm detectors and the prove lane

nodes.name: codefile registration expands globs and honors ignores
nodes.description: codefile add expands the glob against the repo, remembers it for future discovery, and never registers an ignored path unless named explicitly

nodes.name: maturity counts only leaf intents as needing grounding
nodes.description: an intent with hierarchy children is realized via its children; only leaves must ground to code, so a roll-up parent is not reported ungrounded

nodes.name: source structure is extracted per language into symbols imports and metrics
nodes.description: tree-sitter walks rust/python/go/js/ts files into symbols, imports, loc, complexity, nesting and arg counts for the derived plane

nodes.name: changing a file re-opens the asserted edges grounded in it
nodes.description: content-hash ripple: sync stales the asserted edges depending on a changed codefile; an unchanged hash (or a first-ever observation) triggers no ripple, so there is no false churn

nodes.name: an apply batch commits a whole work session atomically
nodes.description: one JSON/YAML file of intents, groundings, relationships, verdicts, adjudications, vocab and tags applies through the normal write gates in a single transaction; any rejection rolls all of it back

nodes.name: iso5055-rel-resource-release
nodes.description: every acquired resource is released on all paths, including errors

detection_hints: in Rust, prefer RAII guards; a manual release missing on an early return is a leak

evidence_template.failing: src/<file>:<line> — resource not released on the error path
evidence_template.passing: src/<file>:<lines> — resources held by RAII guards, released on all paths

failing_example.criterion: connections acquired in the import path are released on every exit
failing_example.evidence: src/import.rs:52 — early return on parse error skips `conn.close()` at line 71

body.inspection_guide: 1. Find resource acquisition (files, locks, connections, handles). 2. Confirm release on all paths (RAII/Drop, defer, finally). 3. A leak on the error path is a violation.

passing_example.criterion: connections acquired in the import path are released on every exit
passing_example.evidence: src/import.rs:30-75 — connection wrapped in an RAII guard; both early returns drop it

nodes.name: iso5055-main-no-dead-or-duplicate-code
nodes.description: no unreachable or unused code; no copy-pasted logic where one definition belongs

detection_hints: red flag: the same logic copy-pasted in two places

evidence_template.passing: src/<file> — no dead code; shared logic factored

failing_example.criterion: the grounded files contain no unreachable functions or duplicated logic
failing_example.evidence: src/util.rs:120-160 duplicates src/io.rs:40-80 line-for-line (same retry loop)

body.inspection_guide: 1. Look for unreachable/unused functions. 2. Look for duplicated logic across files. 3. Significant duplication or dead code is a violation.

passing_example.criterion: the grounded files contain no unreachable functions or duplicated logic
passing_example.evidence: src/util.rs — every function referenced; the shared parse helper is defined once and imported

nodes.name: max-file-size
nodes.description: a file should not exceed a maintainable line count

nodes.name: iso5055-rel-no-unchecked-failure
nodes.description: every fallible operation's failure path is handled or explicitly propagated

detection_hints: red flag: a Result discarded without handling

evidence_template.passing: src/<file>:<lines> — failures propagated via ? or handled explicitly

failing_example.criterion: every fallible call in the payment path propagates or handles its error
failing_example.evidence: src/pay.rs:57 — `let _ = charge(card)` discards the charge failure

body.inspection_guide: 1. Find fallible calls (Result/Option, IO, parsing). 2. Confirm each failure is handled or propagated with `?`. 3. A swallowed error (unwrap_or_default on a real failure, ignored Result) is a violation.

passing_example.criterion: every fallible call in the payment path propagates or handles its error
passing_example.evidence: src/pay.rs:40-92 — all 6 fallible calls use ? or match on Err; no discarded Result
